text: You have a girlfriend who had some crazy past connected to drug using and hanging out with some shady people. And of course she was involved with this one guy who keeps reaching out to her even today. That annoys you and you don't know how to handle the situation. Let's go to the question from one of my subscribers. Hi, I really appreciate your content and the way you analyze relationship situations, so I wanted to share something that has been weighing heavily on me. Before my girlfriend and I ever met, she kissed and was briefly involved with a guy who worked at the same place as us. She never had real feelings for him, either then or now, but he did and still does. At that time, they and a few mutual friends also started using drugs together, which was part of their connection. Now my girlfriend and I are in a relationship and she has completely stepped away from that lifestyle. In a way, I helped her distance herself from drugs and I'm really proud of her for that. However, this same guy still tries to reach out to her, keeps starting conversations and is trying to get her to help him find drugs again. This situation deeply worries me. Knowing they were involved in the past combined with the fact that he still has feelings for her and is trying to pull her back into something she worked hard to leave has been affecting me a lot. I've been losing sleep over it, feeling anxious and unsure how to properly deal with these emotions and boundaries. I trust her, but the situation itself makes me uncomfortable and I don't know what the healthiest way is to handle this. Both for my peace of mind and for our relationship, I would really value your perspective on how to approach this. So this was my answer. Hey man, thanks for kind words, let's go to your situation. Firstly, not sure about real feelings, but she most probably had some feelings for the guy. Girls normally do not kiss or get involved with men they do not have feelings for. Secondly, from the way you write, it is that this dude is a bad guy, he's texting, he has feelings for her, he tries to pull her back. Okay, fine, but do not forget, your girlfriend allows it and that is more important in your situation. To hell with what that guy is doing, much more important is how your girlfriend is reacting. Once again, if you still did not talk to her about it, you should. In a relationship, you should voice if something bothering you. You talk to her, you explain the situation, you tell her how it makes you feel, that it seriously bothers you, makes you uncomfortable, makes you anxious, and then you sit back and observe. If she tells you that she didn't know it, that she's sorry, that she will cut all contact with the guy, ideally block him, then I would say your relationship has a chance. If she tells you, no way she's going to do it, that you are controlling and lack confidence, well, then you have your answer. Your girlfriend at the very least lack empathy towards you, but more realistically, she also doesn't love you, doesn't respect you, doesn't care about your feelings. Then the question is, why would you want to be with a girl like that? To that, he wrote, thank you for your reply, I really took your advice seriously and talked to her openly about everything. She was very clear with me, she has no kind of relationship with him, no interest in him at all, and she doesn't want anything with him. She told me that what truly matters to her is our relationship. She also said that if he still has feelings for her, that is his problem, not hers, and that we won't allow that to interfere with what we have now. She reassured me that she only wants to be with me and hearing that helped me a lot. I just wanted to update you and thank you for pushing me to communicate instead of staying silent. I appreciate your perspective. Once again, guys, another example. If you have a problem, if something bothers you in a relationship, you should voice it, you should talk about it, you shouldn't be silent about it. Then he wrote, there is one more thing I wanted to share, because it is something I'm honestly struggling with. Even though she told me she won't use drugs again, because she knows I don't like it, and because she chose to step away from that life, I still feel afraid sometimes. Not because I don't trust her words, but because addiction and habits can be unpredictable, and that thought stays in my head. What scares me is not only the idea of her using again, but also the uncertainty. If she ever did, how would I even know? That lack of control and clarity makes me anxious, and it's been hard for me to fully relax and sleep peacefully. I don't want to be controlling or suspicious, I just want to know how to deal with this fear in a healthy way, without hurting the relationship or my own mental health. I'd really appreciate your thoughts on this. And that was my answer. Well, once again, you talk to your girlfriend about it. You explain to her that it is really important for you that she stays clean, and do not go back to that life. She needs to understand that it is a priority for you, and that if she does it, she is risking losing you. And you should mean it. You should learn to say things, and go through with it if it happens. So that if you talk to her and say it, and she does it anyways, you end it with her, no matter how hard it is. It is very important as a man to follow through with what you say. And if she feels that you are serious, the chances of her doing it are much lower. I want to say one more thing, man. Maybe you watched my video on relationships. One thing that I say is that relationships should be light and easygoing, or none at all. I am not saying that you should end it with your girlfriend right now, but I am telling you, listen to yourself. If the relationship starts feeling like a struggle, maybe that is your sign. So talk to your girlfriend. If that makes things better, and you can enjoy it, great. If you still would feel anxious, bothered, uneasy, and so on, maybe your own mind tells you something about your relationship. He answered, we already talked about it, and I made it very clear how important this is to me, and that it is a boundary I take seriously. She understands that, and promised she won't go back to that life. Now all that's left is to see if she follows through on her promise. I feel genuinely good with her, and with the way she is. She's an incredible woman, and honestly, drags were the only real red flag I saw. If she truly leaves that behind and stays clean, I believe things can work out well, and that we can continue our path together in a healthy way. That's what I'm hoping for. Thank you again for your perspective and guidance. And with that, I wrote, okay man, I genuinely wish you luck in your relationship. Hope it works out. Just don't be naive and indulge in wishful thinking. Look at person's action, do what is in your control, and then react accordingly. So that was this story. Once again, guys, if something bothers you, don't be afraid to talk about it. I hope this was interesting and informative. My name is Ilya Savdulya. Thanks a lot, and bye.
